Author: dajoey
Name: PvP Solver
Description: PvP-only auto-rotation for FFXIV. Activates in PvP zones.
Changelog:
v0.1.2.15 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.2.14 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.


- **Removed the AI decision layer.** The optional relayed decision model (focus picking, Limit Break firing and the healer-call shadow lines, with their "call the shots" settings row and its relay address field) is gone from the plugin. No fight snapshot is built or sent anywhere anymore, and the plugin makes no decision calls of any kind.
- Targeting, Guard, Recuperate, the defensive table, StickyTarget and every other rotation behavior are unchanged. The defensive rules keep reading real HP (current HP out of the maximum) under the neutral name `RealHp.HpRatio`; no threshold or default moved.
- PvP Solver still never moves the character and never fires a PvP Limit Break on its own logic, exactly as before.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.


- **The Jev co-pilot logs the plain code rule's answer beside Jev's, for both of its questions.** Each `JV|focus-pick` line names the enemy Jev picked and the enemy the plain rule would pick (the lowest-HP enemy in attack range); each `JV|lb-shadow` line names Jev's Limit Break call and the code rule's. Both answers are recorded side by side and graded after the session, to show which one decides better. Log only: targeting, Limit Break firing and every other behavior are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.


- Upstream engine sync (RotationSolverReborn a560469db): the rotation engine now builds in upstream's merged single-project layout.
- Ports upstream engine fixes: the action manager is read at call time instead of a pointer cached at startup (a stale-pointer crash class), configuration saves are atomic (write to a temp file, then replace), and the shield-value calculation can no longer overflow on very large HP values.
- No rotation behavior change; the 21 PvP rotations and their presets are untouched.

v0.1.2.10 (2026-11-01) [testing]
- **The per-job defensive actions also read real HP.** Heart of Corundum, Tempera Coat, Earth's Reply, Riddle of Earth, the Bloodbath rows, Lady of Crowns, Microcosmos, Meisui, Impalement, Xenoglossy's low-HP arm and Shadowbringer's HP arm compared their "use below this HP" thresholds against predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way; predicted can read 84% one second before a death at about 40% real HP. They now compare against the current HP out of the maximum, the same real value Guard and the defensive table already use. Thresholds and defaults are unchanged, and reads of enemies' and allies' HP (Smite, Guardian, Blasting Zone, Perfectio, the burst target) are untouched.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.9 (2026-11-01) [testing]
- **Self-defence now reads real HP.** Guard, Recuperate and the generic defensive actions (the "use below X% HP" table) compared their thresholds against predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way; predicted can read 84% one second before a death at about 40% real HP, so nothing fired. All of them now compare against the current HP out of the maximum, the same real value the Jev snapshot uses. Thresholds and defaults are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.8 (2026-10-31) [testing]
- **"Let Jev call the shots" now sees real HP.** The player's and allies' HP sent to Jev is the current HP out of the maximum, no longer PvP Solver's predicted HP, which counts heals still on the way. In one match Jev was told 84% one second before a death at about 40%.
- **Jev's pick no longer drops when Jev is briefly unsure.** The relay now keeps the last pick itself while that enemy is still hittable, and drops it on purpose when the enemy goes under Guard, out of reach or stale. PvP Solver follows the relay's call and never brings a dropped pick back. Only with an older relay does PvP Solver keep the last pick, for up to three seconds after Jev gave it, while that enemy is still a valid target.
- **The Limit Break log matches what happened.** `JV|lb-fired` is written once when the Limit Break goes off in a fire window. `JV|lb-fire-skip` is written only when a window closes without it, with the reason: unusable, follow-up, out-of-range, no-target or timeout. A report of the use that arrives up to two seconds late still counts as fired. Before, a skip line could appear in windows that then fired, and windows that really failed wrote nothing.
- **Each action used is reported once.** The game reports each action twice; the same action on the same target within 1.5 seconds now counts once in the snapshot.
- **Alliance members are included (Frontline).** After the party members, the nearest alliance members are sent too, marked as alliance, up to eight allies in all. Each ally now carries its object id, so Jev can name an ally to heal.
- **Healer call, logged only.** When Jev suggests whom a healer should heal (an ally, self, attack or Guard), the suggestion is written as one `JV|heal-shadow` log line for the first suggestion in each fight and each time it changes; an answer with no suggestion does not count as a change. Nothing acts on it yet.
- **Relay failures are visible in the log.** One summary line per fight (when combat ends, or every 60 seconds while calls fail) counts calls that succeeded, timed out, got an error reply or failed. No line per call, and no call is counted in a later fight. An unreadable heal or Limit Break value in a reply no longer drops the rest of the answer.
- PvP Solver still never moves the character.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.7 (2026-10-29) [testing]
- **"Let Jev call the shots" reports what actually happened.** Each snapshot also carries the player's current target and the actions actually used since the last one (action and target only), so each of Jev's picks can be checked against what PvP Solver did and whether that enemy went down.
- Jev's focus pick is kept steady: it moves to another enemy only when that one is clearly the better pick.
- **A line, cone or splash Limit Break that Jev called could be skipped** because the action kept its own "most enemies" target. It is now aimed at the enemy Jev chose, which the game has just confirmed as a valid target. A skipped fire writes one reason line to the log.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

Author: dajoey
Name: AutoPotion
Punchline: Per-job HP, MP, and deep dungeon potion automation.
Description: Auto-uses the highest-tier HP potion, MP potion (Ether), and the deep dungeon regen potion (Sustaining / Eurekan / Orthos / Pilgrim's) at configurable thresholds. Each potion's threshold and on/off state is stored per-job, so casters and tanks can have completely different setups.
Changelog:
v0.2.5.4 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The settings window has been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents across every page. All settings, presets and automation behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.2.5.3 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.2.5.2 (2026-10-10) [testing]
- **Automatic item uses no longer cancel an open action sequence.** Any potion, ether, deep dungeon medicine or Echo Drops that would land while mudra seals or Ten Chi Jin are held is delayed until the sequence completes, instead of cancelling the ninjutsu mid-chain. The delay lasts only while the sequence is up (a mudra window is about six seconds) and lifts immediately after; at or below 25% HP the heal fires regardless - a cancelled jutsu is cheaper than dying. No other job's behaviour changes.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- With the optional decision log enabled, a held use is recorded with the `heldmudra` near-miss reason, rate-limited like every other near-miss line.

v0.2.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the master switch, "Only in combat", "Only in a duty", the HP, MP and Regen potion switches with their thresholds, and Cure Silence (Echo Drops) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- The potion settings apply to the active job's profile, as in the settings window.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.2.5.0 (2026-09-05)

- New per-job option: "Auto-use Echo Drops when silenced". When it is on and Silence lands (mob silence spells, AoE silences, deep dungeon traps), AutoPotion uses Echo Drops from inventory to cure it automatically. Item use is not blocked by Silence, so the cure works exactly when nothing else can.
- OFF by default like every option, and per job like the rest: tick the new box in the settings window for the jobs it should apply to. With it off (the default) nothing changes - not even a status check.
- It reuses the same machinery as the potions: HQ Echo Drops are preferred over normal ones, the shared 750 ms cooldown after any potion use applies, and a Silence that arrives during that cooldown is cured on the next tick.
- If the diagnostic tap is enabled, the cure logs as an `e` event; when it cannot fire the near-miss reasons are `edblocked` (on cooldown / blocked) or `ednostock` (none in the bags).
- No change to potion behaviour. HP/MP/regen thresholds, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before.

v0.2.4.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added an optional "Log potion decisions" diagnostic, OFF by default. Turn it on with `/autopotion telemetry on` or the new Advanced / Diagnostics section of the settings window, and AutoPotion writes one line to its plugin log every time it uses a potion, plus a rate-limited line when a threshold was crossed and nothing fired.
- Purpose: the log line records the HP%, the MP%, the threshold that was in force and the job, so a threshold can be verified after the fact instead of guessed at. Nothing leaves the machine - the lines only go to the local Dalamud plugin log.
- The "nothing fired" lines say WHY in a short code: `hpover` (a potion was available but the heal would have been wasted), `hpblocked` / `mpblocked` / `rgblocked` (on cooldown or blocked by a status), `hpnostock` / `mpnostock` / `rgnostock` (none left in inventory) and `rgrehab` (Rehabilitation still up in a deep dungeon).
- These lines are heavily rate-limited on purpose: a repeated state logs once, not once per frame. Measured against 214 minutes of real play the near-miss lines come out under one line per minute, so the log stays readable.
- No change to potion behaviour. Thresholds, per-job profiles, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before, and with the setting off (the default) the plugin does not even build a log line.

Author: dajoey
Name: Armoire Auto-Fill
Punchline: Per-dungeon view of which armoire-eligible gear pieces you're still missing
Description: Lists every armoire-eligible dungeon drop in the game and shows whether each is in your inventory, in your armoire, or still missing. Sort by level, hide completed dungeons, toggle to show owned items too. Open the armoire UI at an inn once per session to populate the in-armoire state; in-inventory and equipped state is detected automatically.
Changelog:
v0.5.7.2 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.5.7.1 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.5.7.0 (2026-10-10)
- **The PvP shopping list now includes gear sold for Trophy Crystals and Wolf Collars.** The crystal quartermaster's Trophy Crystal Exchange (weapons, armour, accessories) and the collar quartermaster's exchange were missing from the list because their cost currencies were not mapped, so the PvP code came out empty. Both quartermasters are in the list now, checked against Knightshopper's own vendor catalog: every exported pair is one it accepts.
- Pieces no import code can name are now listed in the window by name with the reason (the shop has no vendor link in the game data, or Knightshopper has no vendor for its shop), instead of being dropped quietly. The Wolf Mark gear behind the mark quartermaster falls in this list: its shop opens through a dialogue handler, so no vendor pair can be written for it.
- The shopping summary line showed placeholder braces instead of the counts; it shows the numbers now.

v0.5.6.0 (2026-10-08)
- **Import codes now carry only what can actually be bought today.** Some pieces are gated behind more than a quest: seasonal vendors also gate pieces on an achievement, and the previous filter only knew about quests, so pieces the game would not sell yet were still written into the codes, and the first one of them made Knightshopper refuse the whole import ("Item N is not available from its shared Gil vendor"). The shopping list now checks live quest and achievement progress: what can be bought now goes into the code, a piece whose cheapest listing is locked falls back to a listing that can be bought, and a piece with no buyable listing at all is left out and counted at the bottom of the window ("N missing piece(s) need quest or achievement progress you don't have yet - left out of the import"). The rule applies to every currency, not just gil.

v0.5.5.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **Import codes now name vendors that Knightshopper itself has.** The previous build still produced Gil codes that Knightshopper refused whole ("Item N is not available from its shared Gil vendor"): the rule it used to decide which vendors Knightshopper knows was a guess and was wrong for most Gil shops. The rule now follows how Knightshopper builds its own vendor list: a vendor is an NPC the game actually places in an area, and seasonal NPCs that are re-used under new ids with the same name and the same shops count once. It applies to every currency, not just gil. The Gil code now carries several times as many pieces, because shops the old rule dropped by mistake are back.
- Placeholder items with no name are no longer put in a code; Knightshopper has no entry for them.
- Every code and every catalog entry was checked offline against the vendor data produced by Knightshopper's own library (not against this plugin's own model): no refusals. This is not yet confirmed in the game, and newer game patches than the one checked are not covered.
- The shopping-list section says what the codes were checked against and that it is not yet confirmed in-game; the copy message also explains that Knightshopper names only the first item it refuses.
- The vendor placement is read from the game's area files once per session in the background (about one second), with one log line.

v0.5.4.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **Import codes no longer contain items Knightshopper would refuse.** Knightshopper rejects a whole import when even one item is not in its own catalog, which the previous Gil code hit: shops whose vendors only spawn for an event never enter Knightshopper's catalog, but this plugin was still naming them. The catalog now only names shops with a permanently placed vendor, matching how Knightshopper derives its own list, and the same rule applies to every currency, not just gil.
- Pieces that this leaves out are no longer silent: the window shows "N items left out: Knightshopper cannot buy them", the build log counts the skipped shops, and the copy buttons never produce a code Knightshopper would answer with "not available from its shared vendor".

Author: dajoey
Name: Gluttony Combo
Punchline: Lalalazy fork of Wrath Combo - XIVCombo for very lazy players.
Description: Gluttony Combo - lalalazy fork of Gluttony Combo. XIVCombo for very lazy players.
Changelog:
v1.0.4.339 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v1.0.4.338 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v1.0.4.337 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **The AI decision layer is gone.** The Fight Brain's question side - the raidwide mitigation ask, the pre-pull plan reader (party finder text and the `/gluttony plan` note command), and the party-callout reader - has been removed from the plugin, together with its relay address setting and the two "Plan Reader"/"Callout Reader" switches. GluttonyCombo no longer asks any decision model anything, sends no snapshot anywhere, and keeps no relay URL: the only network path it still uses is the movement tap's `/move/ingest` upload, which records the movement profiles and never carried a decision.
- What stays is pure code and unchanged: the rotation and every combo, the Fight Brain forecast reads and `FB|forecast` lines, the countdown strip, the shadow cast-gate lines, the party-data shadow rules (`FB|party-mit`, `FB|pos-zone`), and the movement recorder and shadow move planner. The move planner's `MP|` decision lines keep their exact format and now always carry the code pick only.
- The shadow move planner no longer has its ask-side toggle; `/gluttony movelog` now switches the recorder and the planner together, and its status line reads two switches instead of three.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.336 (2026-11-09) [testing]
- **Saving a custom action to a hotbar while in PvP now writes the PvP layout.** The custom-action editor's hotbar save told the game the write was a normal-slot write regardless of the current content, so a save made while in PvP updated the regular hotbar set instead of the PvP one; the call now passes the content check (upstream's fix), so the PvP variant of the slot is the one written.
- **The action-replacing hook answers in the game's own yes/no shape.** The IsActionIdReplaceable detour and its delegate declared an unsigned 64-bit return where the game's callback uses a boolean, so the replace decision relied on 0/1 marshalling to land correctly; both signatures now match the native BOOL return (upstream's fix), and the early-return values read true/false instead of 1/0. No behavior change is intended - this removes a latent hook-contract mismatch.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.335 (2026-11-07) [testing]
- **AoE heals no longer fire back to back on a party that is at or near full HP.** Follow-up to 1.0.4.334: on a party whose bars all read full or nearly full, the auto-rotation kept pressing AoE heals - a bar just under 100% never counted as full (regen-tick oscillation and display rounding), and a heal that had just gone out did not stand the press path down while it landed. Two changes, shared by Astrologian, White Mage, Scholar and Sage. First, a member only counts as needing an AoE heal on a real deficit: a bar at or above 98% reads as full for both the one-button average and the auto-rotation's member count, so no threshold setting (including the 100 "disable this check" setting, and a target count of 0, which is now floored at 1) can make a full party eligible. Second, the auto-rotation presses one AoE heal at a time: after a press goes out, the next waits out that cast's flight plus a second for the heal to land and party HP to propagate, so a movement-cancelled cast is no longer re-issued every tick. Real damage is never starved - a party still under the threshold after the window heals again immediately. Single-target heals, raidwide pre-casts and the 1.0.4.334 out-of-range fix are unchanged; the manual one-button still heals when pressed.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.334 (2026-11-07) [testing]
- **Healer one-button AoE heals no longer trigger off party members the heal cannot reach.** The Astrologian, White Mage, Scholar and Sage one-button AoE heal rotations averaged the whole party's HP: a member standing outside the heal's radius kept the average under the threshold, so the rotation kept choosing AoE heals (Helios, Medica, Succor, Prognosis and their oGCD neighbours) that could never heal that member. The trigger now averages only the members inside the heal's own effect radius (15y for the Helios family), alive and targetable, so the rotation returns to damaging while nobody reachable needs healing, and heals again the moment the far member comes back into range. Single-target healing is untouched: a member returning to range is picked up by the single-target path exactly as before. Raidwide pre-casts and the auto-rotation's own cast gate are unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

Author: croizat, dajoey
Name: Lazy Fate Automation
Punchline: Fully automated FATE grinding utilizing vnavmesh, lifestream, and Gluttony Combo.
Description: Automates FATE grinding, including Zodiac Atma, Anima Luminous Crystals, Resistance Memories, Phantom Demiatmas, Yo-kai Watch Medals, and Bicolor Gemstones. Seamlessly integrates with vnavmesh for pathing and flight, lifestream for zone swapping, TextAdvance for dialogue skipping, and Gluttony Combo/BossMod for combat. Use /lazyfate to open.
Changelog:
v0.0.3.12 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.0.3.11 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.0.3.10 (2026-10-31) [testing]
- **The FATE grind no longer starts FATEs above your level.** Level sync only lowers your level to match a FATE, it never raises it, so a FATE above your level could not be contributed to and walking to it only wasted time. FATEs above your level are now skipped; the tracker's unavailable list shows "FATE level N is above your level M". FATEs at or below your level run exactly as before.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.0.3.9 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **Display name format and sort order changes are now saved.** Edits in the FATE tracker's "Sorting & Display" settings previously lived only in memory and reverted on the next plugin load; every change now persists immediately.
- **Reset to Default restores the actual default sort order.** The reset button dropped the Time Remaining criterion and put Time Remaining Urgent in ascending order (urgent FATEs last); it now restores the shipped six-entry default, shared with the config's own default so the two cannot drift apart.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.0.3.8 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **BossMod Reborn no longer runs its own job rotations beside Gluttony Combo during FATEs.** The FATE grind creates and uses its own BossMod preset, "LazyFateAutomation", holding only the movement, FATE-targeting, level-sync and stay-close-to-target modules (melee and tanks close in, other roles hold at 10 yalms), and rewrites it each time the grind starts so an old or edited copy cannot bring job rotations back.
- **The grind no longer clears a BossMod preset another plugin (such as AutoDuty) or the player set.** It turns its preset on and off with BossMod Reborn's standard preset calls and only ever clears its own. Two calls BossMod Reborn does not provide, which failed on every attempt, are gone, and a failing call is logged once per run.
- The BossMod preset named "Gluttony" that earlier versions created is no longer used. It is left untouched in BossMod's preset list and can be deleted there by hand.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.0.3.7 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The boss FATE icon on the server info bar entry now actually renders.** The previous testing build showed no icon at all because the glyph reference pointed at an empty slot instead of the boss FATE icon; the icon value is now pinned so it stays the boss glyph.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Click behavior, the confirming second click and every other part of the server bar entry are unchanged.

Author: dajoey
Name: Lazy Skyward Tracker
Punchline: Track your Skyward points for all jobs toward the Pteranodon mount
Description: Tracks all jobs' Skyward points for the Pteranodon mount achievement. Scans your inventory for Skybuilders turn-in items and projects how many points they'll add, shown as a cyan bar extension on each job's progress bar. Use /lazysky to open.

Author: dajoey
Name: Lazy Fish Sitter
Punchline: Sits you down while you fish. That's it.
Description: Checks every few seconds while you are fishing; if you are not sitting, it runs /sit for you. Leaves you alone once you are seated (ground sit, chair, or pose).
Changelog:
v0.1.5.3 (2026-11-14) [testing]
- The plugin windows have been rebuilt on the shared LalaUiKit: one consistent layout with themed section headers, unified spacing and colour accents. All settings and behaviour are unchanged, and existing configuration loads as-is.

v0.1.5.2 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the "Sit while fishing" switch to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.5.0 (2026-09-25)

- Persistent seating across fishing hole visits: if the character stands up during a visit to a fishing hole (such as putting the rod away to change bait or use cordials, or manually standing up), the automation now detects the stand and re-seats upon resuming fishing or on the subsequent cast.
- Unaccepted send cap: the 3-send limit per hole visit is now scoped to consecutive unaccepted sends rather than a lifetime cap per hole visit. When a sit is accepted by the game, the counter resets, ensuring long fishing sessions with multiple bait changes or pauses remain seated while still guarding against unbounded retry loops if commands are blocked.

v0.1.4.0 (2026-09-25)

- Sits after a cast: the automated /sit check now runs after a cast once the line is settled in the water (`LineInWater`), in addition to the pre-cast standby beat (`PoleReady`). In active fishing loops or when using automated casting tools, the standby beat between casts typically lasts under a second, which previously prevented the automation from ever triggering across repeated casts (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- Safe timing: commands are sent only after the line has been in the water for at least 1 second to ensure the cast animation has resolved, and continue to be refused during active casting, biting, hooking, reeling, and position change animations.

v0.1.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Correction first, because the last release's notes got the game wrong: FFXIV does NOT force standing on every hooked fish. If the character is sitting when the cast starts, the game keeps it seated for the whole loop - a hook may cause a momentary stand, but the game sits back down on its own. v0.1.2.0 was designed around that mistake (one /sit per cast) and this release replaces it entirely.
- Sit once, then stay out of the way. The plugin now sends a single /sit per fishing trip, at a moment the game will actually accept it, and then does nothing for the rest of the trip (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`).
- That moment is the standby beat: rod out, no line in the water (`FishingEventHandler.State == PoleReady`), held for a second, at least 3 seconds clear of a bite/hook/reel, with the character read as standing for 3 seconds straight. It will never fire mid-cast, with a line in the water, mid-bite, mid-reel, or while already sitting down or standing up (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsStandbyBeat`).
- That is why v0.1.1.0 looked like it did nothing: it sent its one /sit the instant the fishing flag came on, which is after the line is already out, and the game swallows the emote there - ten sends across ten sessions, no effect. v0.1.2.0 still counted "line in water" as a valid moment and would have done the same thing.
- No re-sit after every cast, ever. A brief standing read just after a bite, hook, reel or collectable prompt is treated as the game's own animation, not as the character standing up, so the plugin does nothing and lets the game re-seat (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `IsHookish`).
- A "trip" is one visit to a fishing hole, not one cast. The fishing flag drops between casts (v0.1.1.0 saw ten "sessions" in 21 minutes), so the limits are now anchored to the hole and only reset after 20 seconds away from it (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `StartTrip` / `EndTrip`).
- Anti-yo-yo guards, all hard, because a /sit on a seated character STANDS them: never sends while any seated signal reads seated; at least 10 seconds between sends; at most 3 sends per trip with a log line when it stops; and once the game has taken a sit this trip it will not send again unless the seated read has proved it still reports seated with the rod out (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `Decide`, guards 1-5).
- The settings window now shows the trip counters: whether the character is at a hole, sits used out of 3, whether the game took the sit, and whether the seated read works while fishing (file: `ConfigWindow.cs`).
- Removed the "check interval" slider. The plugin now looks every frame, because every limit that matters is a real time limit (10 seconds between sends, 3 seconds of standing before it believes the read, 3 sends a trip) and a 2-second poll just made it step over short standby beats between quick casts. Saved values are ignored, not lost (files: `ConfigWindow.cs`, `Configuration.cs`).
- The policy is now a plain C# class with no game code in it (`Core/SitPolicy.cs`), replayed offline against 26 scripted fishing sessions by `tests/LazyFishSitter.Harness`. Three releases in a row shipped a rule that only broke in game; the harness caught three more before this one shipped, including a dead window that would have stopped a refused /sit from ever being retried.
- Keeps the detailed state logging (every fishing-state and posture change, 40 lines a minute max) and adds a one-line trip summary, so the still-open question - does the game ever report seated while a line is out - can be answered from the log without typing anything in game (file: `FishSitService.cs`, `EndTrip`).

Author: dajoey
Name: LazyRetainerLive
Punchline: Real-time retainer venture countdowns for your dashboard.
Description: Serves the logged-in character's live retainer and venture state on loopback HTTP (127.0.0.1:10504) so the ffxiv dashboard relay can show real-time venture countdowns instead of AutoRetainer's occasionally-stale file cache.
Changelog:
v0.1.0.3 (2026-11-10) [testing]
- Rebuilt against the Dalamud 15.0.4.0 payload for game patch 7.58. No functional changes.

v0.1.0.2 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the switch that serves retainer data (the port stays in the plugin's own window) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.1.0.1 (2026-09-05)


- Corrected a wrong claim in the v0.1.0.0 notes below (and on the mod's web page): **the endpoint does not answer 503 on logout.** Once logged in, it keeps serving that character's last known retainer state - including at the title screen - and only ever answers 503 if it has never read the retainer table at all since the plugin loaded (i.e. it started at the title screen and no login has happened yet). That freeze is deliberate and is the better behaviour: measured previously the frozen live snapshot was still *newer* than AutoRetainer's file, so falling back to the file on logout would have shown the dashboard **older** data, not fresher. No behaviour was changed here - only the description was wrong.
- The settings window no longer reports "serving live snapshot" while logged out. It now distinguishes three states: no snapshot yet, serving a live snapshot, or serving the last-known snapshot while the game is in transition.


- For anything scripting against this endpoint: `readAt` is the time the request was **served**, not the time the data was read from the game, so it does not reveal how stale a frozen snapshot is. Use the settings window (or `/lazyretainerlive debug`) to tell live from frozen.

v0.1.0.0 (2026-09-05)


- First release. LazyRetainerLive reads the logged-in character's LIVE retainer table (the same in-memory data AutoRetainer uses to drive its own countdowns) and serves it as JSON on `http://127.0.0.1:10504/retainers`, so the ffxiv dashboard's retainer panel can show venture countdowns that update the moment a venture is collected instead of whenever AutoRetainer next saves its config file.
- When not logged in (or the live table has no data yet) the endpoint answers HTTP 503, which tells the dashboard relay to fall back to AutoRetainer's file. Loopback only - the port is never reachable from other machines.


- Companion of AutoRetainer - it reads, it never writes, assigns, or collects anything. Settings: Enabled (default on) and loopback port (default 10504). Commands: `/lazyretainerlive` opens settings, `/lazyretainerlive debug` dumps listener + snapshot state, `/lazyretainerlive changelog` reopens this popup.
- Why this exists: AutoRetainer's `DefaultConfig.json` (which feeds the dashboard today) is saved only at AutoRetainer's own save points, so its venture rows can be tens of minutes stale while ventures are actually completing. The countdown for the logged-in character lives in the game's memory - this plugin is a small read-only window onto it.

- **"Score: three familiars" run-roster mode, off by default.** For score runs. A run roster of one to three familiars scores the Beast Squad III bonus on every board, so with the option on the run roster is the best three familiars for the whole board instead of the board's full roster. The three are chosen from the familiars you own and that are not knocked out: they cover as many of the board's required interrupt, dispel and cleanse needs as any three can, then the damage the board calls to be blunted, then three of one kin when that costs no required cover (the Gambit bonus), then the rest by points. A roster of three saved for a different board is rewritten for the board you enter. Whatever the three cannot answer on the board is named on the window's summary line; nothing pops up. With three or fewer familiars the game registers the battlehorns itself, so the plugin leaves them alone. Found in the settings window and the Lazy Hub as "Score: three familiars".

- **Works with AutoDuty.** While AutoDuty runs, it handles the run roster, shop, treasure, spoils and campsite itself, so the plugin stands by there; the battlehorns are AutoDuty's only with its "Fight picks" on, and the plugin picks them otherwise. AutoDuty's active profile is read through AutoDuty's own interface (its config file when that is unavailable), never changed; when neither can be read, every screen stands by, as before. The window shows one quiet line naming the screens it is standing by on.
- **No more corrections on top of AutoDuty's familiar picks.** AutoDuty re-applied its own picks every time, so they never reached a fight.
- **Fight guide: the Snarl -> Parting Blow advice is gone** (Parting Blow no longer dodges a hit since the September 17 hotfix). Plain tankbusters say to let a familiar with enough HP take them under Snarl; poisoning ones (Deadly Thrust, Cold Caress, Toxic Vomit) say to Parting Blow right after the hit so the poison leaves with the familiar; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration says to save the Blink tome for it.
- Item values: Beastly Knife is valued like the elemental axes; Hero's Crown counts its Excellence proc (9 s of nullified attacks); Rapid Recast gear is valued; reraise items are worth a little less at Third Degree.
- **Patch 7.57: battlehorns the game registered itself (teams of three or fewer) are left alone**; a knocked-out member of a three-familiar team is no longer toggled off the horns.
- **Patch 7.57: the board's degree survives a job change** (the game now keeps the Crucible Mode until logout), so the degree passed to Gluttony Combo is no longer reset when the character returns to Beastmaster. It is forgotten at logout.
